subject: Verification sprint: onboarding plan for Quality monitoring and rollback policy
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Ahmed <samira@verdant.ai>, Lucas Meyer <lucas@verdant.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Verification sprint: onboarding plan for Quality monitoring and rollback policy

Hi Samira / Lucas,

Great to meet briefly on the demo yesterday — thanks for the time. As discussed, we want to lock down the first "verification sprint" scope so Verdant can get prompt-level regression monitoring and an eval harness integrated into staging before the production rollout. Proposed high-level plan below: please confirm or flag changes.

Scope (week 1):
- Ingest and map your initial prompt sets (attached Verdant_promptset_v1.csv) and label owner/intent tags.
- Wire the eval harness (attached eval_harness_config.yaml) into your staging pipeline; Redwood will provide the harness adapter and a sample CI job.
- Configure two alert tiers: soft regressions (investigate) and tripwires (auto rollback).

Proposed tripwire / rollback basics:
- Canary: staged traffic at 10% for 48h with active monitoring.
- Tripwire trigger: defined regression set sees >=5% increase in failure rate OR average similarity score drops by >0.08 vs baseline over a 24h window.
- Rollback action: automatic rollback to pinned model variant and page the oncall + CS lead.

Owners & meeting cadence:
- Verdant: Samira (CS owner), Lucas (platform eng)
- Redwood: Marissa (CS implementation), Lauren (integrations/engineer), Soojin (quality ops)
- Daily sync during the sprint (15 min), handoff notes at sprint close.

Deliverables attached: promptset CSV, harness config, and a short runbook template (qmon_runbook_v1.md). Can we lock a kickoff for next Tue 09:00 PT? If that works, Lauren and Soojin will lead the integration steps.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: eval_harness_config.yaml (yaml)]

From: Samira Ahmed <samira@verdant.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lucas Meyer <lucas@verdant.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Verification sprint: onboarding plan for Quality monitoring and rollback policy

Thanks Aditya — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications from our side before kickoff:

1) Compliance window: we need the eval harness logs to be retained 180 days for our audits. Can Redwood's harness adapter include a configurable retention param?
2) Tripwire thresholds: 5% increase sounds reasonable but can we tie that to weighted critical intents first? We have a few high-risk prompts (payment, PHI-extraction) that should be stricter.

We're happy to run the mapping exercise for prompt owners tomorrow and will upload an updated CSV with intent priority tags. Kickoff Tue 09:00 PT works for Samira + Lucas.

—Samira
Customer Success, Verdant AI
[Attachment: verdant_prompt_priority_draft.csv (csv)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Verification sprint: onboarding plan for Quality monitoring and rollback policy

Internal notes / proposed tweaks before we present at kickoff — will paste into the runbook and share the link:  https://drive.redwood.example/drive/verdant-qmon/runbook

- Retention: we can parameterize the harness to push logs to Verdant's S3 with lifecycle 180d; need Lucas to confirm bucket access and KMS key.
- Tiered tripwires: propose two-tier thresholds per intent priority:
  * High-risk intents: 2.5% regression or similarity drop >0.05 -> immediate alert to oncall + CS; 4h investigation SLA before rollback decision.
  * Medium/low: 5% / 0.08 similarity -> investigate; automated rollback only if accompanied by steady drift across two consecutive windows.
- Canary plan detail: start with a control window (no traffic split) to establish baseline over 24h, then 10% split for 48h. If metric drift > tripwire, flag and pause the split automatically.
- Eval harness integration: Lauren will own the CI job that runs the harness nightly against the regression set and uploads a summary report to the shared Drive. Soojin will own the alert definitions inside Redwood's monitoring console.

Next steps I will cover on the call: sprint checklist, sample regression queries, runbook walkthrough, rollback playbook (who clicks what), and doc ownership.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Implementation Lead, Redwood
[Attachment: qmon_runbook_v1.md (markdown)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Ahmed <samira@verdant.ai>, Lucas Meyer <lucas@verdant.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 13:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Verification sprint: onboarding plan for Quality monitoring and rollback policy

Samira — thanks, that retention setting is doable. Lucas, when you upload the updated CSV, include the bucket/KMS details and we will add the S3 sink in the harness config.

Quick integration notes for kickoff:
- I will push an initial harness adapter to the Verdant staging repo before Tue and open a PR for the CI job.
- Nightly harness run -> summary JSON + human-friendly report to Drive. We'll include a minimal dashboard for the canary window.
- For rollbacks we'll implement: pinned-variant toggle + a safety net that pauses the canary split if tripwire fires. Manual rollback can be executed in the console and will be part of the runbook steps.

Confirming Tue 09:00 PT for kickoff. I'll be on the call with the adapter PR ready so we can walk through a dry-run.

Lauren Bishop
Integrations Engineer, Redwood Inference
